q: 1. Sinking fund is
options: the fund for rebuilding a structure when its economic life is over
the total sum to be paid to the municipal authorities by the tenants
a part of the money kept in reserve for providing additional structure and structural modifications
explain: A sinking fund is set aside periodically to rebuild or replace a structure at the end of its economic life.

q: 2. The amount saved as depreciation reserve fund will be termed as
explain: It is a reserve set aside for replacement, so it is none of operating cost, profit or loss.

q: 3. Economic saving of time result by crashing
explain: Only critical activities shorten the project, and the cheapest one adds the least cost.

q: 4. Crash project duration is obtained by summing the
options: normal durations for all the activities
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path obtained by taking into account the normal duration for the activities
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path obtained by taking into account the crash duration for all the activities
explain: Crash duration is the sum of crash durations along the critical path, found after all activities are crashed.

q: 5. Indirect cost of the project
options: decrease up to optimum duration and then increase with duration
explain: Indirect cost (overheads) rises with project duration.

q: 6. Total project cost
options: initially reduces and then increases with increase in time
initially increases and then reduces with increase in time
explain: As project duration increases from crash time, direct cost falls while indirect cost rises; the combined total cost initially decreases then increases, forming a U-shaped curve.

q: 7. The total cost versus time curve is
explain: The sum of direct and indirect cost curves against project duration forms a U-shaped curve with a minimum at the optimum duration.

q: 8. Crashing to the project means
options: reducing the time of completion by spending more resources
reducing the cost of project by delaying the time of completion
reducing the project size to save the resources
explain: Crashing means shortening the project completion time by applying additional resources (at extra cost) to critical activities.

q: 9. The time below witch the duration can not be further reduced is known as
explain: Crash time is the absolute minimum time in which an activity can be completed by employing additional resources, regardless of cost.

q: 10. The cost corresponding to the completion of activity within normal time is
explain: Normal cost is the expenditure associated with completing an activity in its 'normal time' using standard resources and methods.

q: 11. Assuming that the cost varies with time, the cost – slope is defined as
options: (crash cost - normal cost) / (normal time - crash time)
explain: Cost slope represents the increase in cost per unit of time saved. It is calculated as the change in cost divided by the change in time.

q: 12. Indirect cost of the project
options: decreases up to optimum duration and then increase with duration
explain: Indirect costs are time-dependent expenses (overheads); the longer the project lasts, the more these costs accumulate.

q: 13. Total project cost
options: initially reduces with time and then increases with further increases
explain: Total cost is the sum of direct and indirect costs. It typically decreases as duration increases toward the 'optimum' point, then starts to rise again as indirect costs dominate.

q: 14. The time corresponding to minimum total project cost is
options: between normal time and crash time
explain: The optimum duration lies between the normal and crash times, where direct plus indirect cost is lowest.

q: 15. The time corresponding to minimum total project cost is
explain: In time-cost optimization, the 'optimum duration' (which minimizes total cost) usually falls between the crash time and normal time, often aligning with the optimistic perspective of cost-efficiency.

q: 16. The time with which direct cost does not reduce with the increase in time is known as
explain: Normal time is the duration beyond which increasing time further does not lead to any further reduction in direct costs.

only on activities lying on the original critical path and having flatter cost slopes
on original critical activities and those that become critical
explain: Per the answer key, c. (The same question appears later with option d as the key answer, in Q175.)

explain: Per the answer key, projects.

21. In time-cost optimization of a project, crashing is done
options: on all the activities lying on the critical path
only on activities lying on the original critical path and having flatter cost slopes
on original critical activities and those that become critical at any stage of crashing in the order of ascending cost slope
explain: Crashing starts with the cheapest critical activity, and activities that become critical later are included.

q: 22. The time with which direct cost does not reduce with the increase in time is known
explain: Per the answer key, normal time, beyond which more time gives no further saving in direct cost.

q: 23. The cost slope is defined as
options: (crash cost - normal cost)/(normal time - crash time)
explain: Cost slope is calculated as (crash cost - normal cost) divided by (normal time - crash time), giving cost increase per unit time reduction.

q: 24. In time-cost optimization of a project, crashing is done.
options: on all the activities lying on the critical path
only on activities lying on the orginal critical path and having flatter cost slopes
on original critical activities and those that become critical at any stage of crashing in the order of ascending cost slope
explain: Crashing in time-cost optimization is applied progressively to critical activities (including newly critical ones as crashing proceeds), always in ascending order of cost slope.

q: 25. Quality control ensures that the physical works conforms to
options: Strength specified in the contract document
Standard specified in the contract document
explain: Quality control ensures the executed work conforms to the standards specified in the contract document.

q: 26. Assuming that the cost varies with time, the cost - slope is defined as
options: \frac{\text{crash cost - normal cost}}{\text{normal time - crash time}}
explain: Cost Slope represents the extra direct cost per unit time saved: $\text{Cost Slope} = \frac{\text{Crash Cost} - \text{Normal Cost}}{\text{Normal Time} - \text{Crash Time}}$.

options: initially reduces and then increases with increase in time
initially increases and then reduces with increase in time
explain: Total cost falls to a minimum at the optimum duration and then rises.

q: 29. Crashing is:

q: 30. Which of the following is an indirect cost in construction work?
options: cost of labour to erect forms
cost of that can be attributed to any single task
explain: Overhead costs (administrative, supervisory) are indirect costs, not directly tied to a specific work item, unlike labour or subcontracted task-specific costs.

q: 31. Sensitivity analysis is a study of
options: change in output due to change in input
economics of cost and benefits of the project
explain: Sensitivity analysis studies how output changes when inputs change.
